title: Prefill Staggered Orchestrator for Heterogeneous SKU fleets (H100 / L40S / A10, MIG-aware)
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a scheduler/orchestrator that staggers prefill work across heterogeneous GPU SKUs and MIG partitions while selecting kernels based on SKU fingerprint + thermal/headroom. Goals: reduce P99 prefill latency regressions introduced by mixed-SKU co-tenancy, avoid thermal-driven throttling spikes, and improve throughput per-dollar by opportunistically packing small token-density requests onto slices without violating latency SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end prefill sequencing that can be enabled via runtime flag `prefill_stagger_v2`
Median prefill latency unchanged and P95/P99 improved by >= 10% for mixed H100/L40S/A10 workloads compared to baseline
No regressions in single-SKU throughput (within 3%) and no new OOMs across MIG partitions
Kernel selection integrates a lightweight kernel-fingerprint cache and falls back to safe kernels when headroom < threshold
Automated benchmark harness (kbench-prefill-mixed) added to CI with representative token-length distribution and SKU mix
comments: 2025-02-14 - Maya Chen: Kickoff. Problem observed in customer sandbox: mixed H100+A10 fleet showed P99 prefill spikes during bursty short requests. Hypothesis: aggressive kernel packing + uniform prefill windows cause thermal cliffs and FIFO stalls on MIG slices.

2025-02-18 - Diego Alvarez: PoC of staggered prefill windows for A10 slices. Built scheduler that defers non-latency-critical prefill lanes by 2-4ms; microbench shows 6% drop in P99 on pure-A10 tests.

2025-02-22 - Experiment: hybrid kernel selector added. It computes SKU fingerprint (SMs, clock cap, mem BW) and consults a tiny on-host cache to pick candidate kernels. Fallback to 'safest' kernel if predicted headroom < 30%. Observed 9% median latency increase in extreme thermal case but eliminated 100% of OOMs in that run.

2025-02-25 - Design review notes (from PM Lucia K): emphasize observability knobs: expose per-route prefilling policy, kernel-choice reason, and headroom estimates to Console trace. Add rollout canary plan to Dedicated customers only.

2025-02-27 - Eng sync: decided to implement three scheduling tiers: immediate (low-latency), deferred-stagger (short defers to adjacent slices), and opportunistic-pack (batch small requests to underutilized slices). Added metrics: prefill_defers, opportunistic_packed_tokens, kernel_fallbacks.

2025-03-01 - Microbench results (kbench-prefill-mixed v0.3): mixed fleet (50% H100-L40S, 50% A10-MIG slices) baseline P99=112ms, staggered orchestrator P99=98ms (12.5% improvement). Cost/unit tokens improved 4% in mixed runs. Latency SLO preserved for immediate tier.
2025-03-02 - PR ready: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7321. Includes scheduler, kernel-cache, and kbench harness. Need QA verification on L40S infra in us-west2.

2025-03-03 - Note from SRE Priya N.: request adding circuit-breaker for when host thermal telemetry degrades under 60% confidence to avoid oscillations between kernels and schedules. Marked as follow-up.
NEXT STEPS: run canary on Dedicated pool with small customer cohort, instrument Console with new prefill metrics, add automated regression alert tied to eval prompts that are latency-sensitive.
experiment_results: kbench-prefill-mixed v0.1 - pure A10-MIG: baseline P99=86ms, staggered P99=80.8ms (-6%).
kbench-prefill-mixed v0.2 - H100+L40S blend: baseline P99=74ms, orchestrator P99=66ms (-11%).
kbench-prefill-mixed v0.3 - mixed fleet including small-token bursts: baseline P99=112ms, orchestrator P99=98ms (-12.5%), median latency +/-3%
Cost per 1M tokens: baseline $21.3, orchestrator $20.45 (~4% reduction) in mixed runs with opportunistic packing enabled.
Kernel fallback rate observed: 0.7% of prefill requests during heavy thermal events. When fallback triggered, P99 prevented from >300ms spikes in reproducible thermal test.
OOMs: baseline reproducible on certain MIG packing patterns; orchestrator eliminated OOMs in 12/12 stress runs.
